Alright, let's cut through the noise. Saturday, November 21, 2026. Here's what's actually going on.

---

**Money Talk**

- **Anthropic IPO tanks, taking tech with it.**
  Anthropic's "historic" Nasdaq debut turned into a bloodbath, colliding with tech's worst week since 2020. Nvidia just closed its longest losing streak since '08, and the whole AI bubble is looking less like a boom and more like a bust as the S&P 500 and Dow hit correction territory. Turns out, gravity still works. [S2][S8][S70]
- **CoreWeave signals AI boom's shaky foundation.**
  The cloud computing company CoreWeave is being called the "poster child of the AI bubble," laden with debt, symbolizing the increasingly risky business model of building massive data centers. All that AI hype needs physical infrastructure, and right now, it looks like a house of cards. [S11]
- **GTA 6 drops, breaks all records.**
  Rockstar just casually dropped GTA 6, and it raked in an insane $3.8 billion in a *single day*. That's the biggest entertainment launch ever, surpassing every video game and film box office record. Forget crypto, just build a virtual world where you can steal cars. [S7]
- **Trump eyes credit card caps, claims FBI hack could expose "hoax."**
  President Trump is looking to cap credit card interest and fees, saying companies "simply make too much money." Also, he’s spinning the recent FBI database hack as a potential "positive," claiming it might expose details of the "Russia Russia Russia hoax." Always focused on the real issues, and his old grievances. [S1][S16][S17]
- **Doomsday economy heats up amidst tech outages.**
  Frequent tech outages are sparking fears of AI cyberattacks and vulnerabilities in the U.S. electricity grid, leading to a surge in the "doomsday economy." Apparently, prepping for the apocalypse is a growth industry now. [S3][S51]

**World Lore**

- **UN talks on killer robots punted, again.**
  Efforts to establish legally binding rules for autonomous weapons have, predictably, gone nowhere. UN talks in Geneva ended with an agreement to just keep talking for another two years, while military AI advances at warp speed. Good to know our leaders are on top of it. [S21][S24]
- **Ukraine left out of Trump's talks with Russia, China.**
  As President Trump chats it up with his Russian and Chinese counterparts, Ukraine and its European allies are noticeably absent from the table. Meanwhile, a family outside Kyiv is bracing for their fifth winter of war, and Russia just struck Zelenskyy's hometown. Some things never change. [S22][S25][S34]
- **EU and UK agree to "Brexit Reset."**
  A deal covering British food exports, emissions trading, and a youth scheme has been struck, with UK politicians now saying rejoining the EU is "on the table" for informal discussions. Apparently, after years of self-inflicted wounds, they're finally remembering what "cooperation" means. [S10][S14][S26]
- **EU inks trade deal with Indonesia, eyes tech giant tax.**
  The EU just signed a massive trade deal with Indonesia, covering 730 million people, aimed at diversifying trade ties. Simultaneously, there's a new EU budget proposal floating around that includes a 3% tax on major digital firms. They want the benefits of trade but also a slice of the tech pie. [S32][S33]
- **Russian helicopter violates Finnish airspace.**
  Finland's Defense Ministry is investigating a suspected Russian helicopter incursion, believed to be linked to a drone strike on a US-sanctioned Russian cargo ship. Old habits die hard, especially for neighbors. [S31]

**Tech Tea**

- **Anthropic's safety-first stance challenged by Wall Street.**
  While Anthropic touts its commitment to AI safety, the reality of an $895 billion compute bill, a costly free tier, and demanding shareholders might make that "no-ads" pledge hard to keep. Money talks, even in AI ethics. [S48][S57]
- **AI agents infiltrating your text messages.**
  A new wave of AI agents are now designed to live directly in your text messages, offering everything from general assistance to specialized help for families, travel, and work. Your phone is about to get even smarter, or at least, a lot more conversational. [S41]
- **Selling your face to AI microdrama? The new Hollywood.**
  Actors are licensing their faces to microdrama startups, a trend already booming in China. Experts are questioning the long-term implications for Hollywood – apparently, not everyone wants to be deepfaked into perpetuity. [S42]
- **Startup sues Apple over tap-to-share.**
  A U.S. startup is going after Apple in India, seeking $162 million in damages and an injunction against iPhone and Apple Watch imports, claiming Apple ripped off their tap-to-share contacts feature. Always a fun legal battle when the little guy takes on Cupertino. [S44]
- **AI experts susceptible to "honey-trap" schemes.**
  Turns out, the brilliant minds building our AI future are just as vulnerable to old-school "honey-trap" schemes. They can protect the world's data, but apparently not their hearts. Classic human vulnerability, never changes. [S45]

**Creator Szn**

- **Consulting firms muscle into marketing's C-suite.**
  Deloitte Digital and Accenture Song are making a fresh push to sell marketing services directly to the C-suite, trying to snag the high-value accounts that traditional holdcos covet. The suits are coming for the creatives, again. [S56]
- **Brands lean into creator-led ad production.**
  Paying creators to make ads for brands is now the fastest-growing segment of the influencer economy. It's cheaper, often more authentic, and clearly more effective than traditional ad agencies. RIP, Mad Men. [S58]
- **OpenAI tweaks ChatGPT Business Hub terms after legal kerfuffle.**
  OpenAI had to rewrite its ChatGPT Business Hub terms because the original legal language raised concerns about restricting businesses' legal claims. Good to know they’re listening, even if it took a minor uproar. [S59]
- **The imperfect shift of TV ads to streaming.**
  While ad budgets are definitely moving from linear TV to streaming, the financial reality behind the shift might not be as smooth or as profitable as some perceive. The streaming gold rush still has some rough edges. [S60]

**Supply Lines**

- **DHL Express streamlines customs with AI product identifier.**
  DHL Express rolled out a new AI-generated product identifier, making customs clearance easier and cutting down on guesswork for small cross-border shippers. This is big for trade friction, reducing delays and headaches at borders. [S62]
- **Groundtruth launches AI platform for freight billing, partners with J.B. Hunt.**
  Startup Groundtruth is tackling the nightmare of freight billing with an AI platform that automates invoice reconciliation. They're nearly fully deployed across J.B. Hunt, and now offering the tech to other carriers, brokers, and forwarders – a serious step towards digitizing antiquated paperwork. [S64]
- **UPS expands healthcare logistics with acquisitions and partnerships.**
  UPS is on a spree, acquiring Smartways Logistics to boost healthcare delivery in Australia and New Zealand, and making another deal in the Asia Pacific. They also partnered with Medvantx for patient delivery. Healthcare is a goldmine for specialized logistics, and UPS is doubling down. [S75][S76][S77][S78]
- **Amazon threatens NYC exit over delivery regulations.**
  Amazon is warning it might pull out of New York City deliveries, escalating a fight with Mayor Zohran Mamdani over regulations and what he calls "Jeff Bezos' greed." This could seriously disrupt last-mile for millions, though some customers are already getting Amazon deliveries from eBay orders, so who knows what's real anymore. [S85][S86][S87][S89]
- **Tentative deal averts strike at Port of LA-Long Beach.**
  A year of bargaining and federal mediation finally paid off, with a tentative union accord easing the immediate threat of a strike at the nation’s busiest container port complex. Dodged a bullet there; a strike would have sent shockwaves through global supply chains. [S61]
- **Holiday shipping getting "spicy" as trucking rejection rates rise.**
  FreightWaves SONAR data shows early signs of a tightening market ahead of Thanksgiving, with trucking tender rejection rates expected to jump over 14%. Low inventory levels are fueling last-minute demands, making capacity scarcer and prices higher. Better order your holiday gifts now, or pay surge pricing. [S65]
- **Railroads maintain right to charge for private car parking.**
  A federal ruling has reinforced railroads' authority to charge for private railcars held at industrial parks, with CSX and Norfolk Southern having collected nearly $1 billion in annual demurrage in 2021. This decision ensures carriers can keep revenue flowing from these fees, even when cars and land are private, which means higher costs for shippers using rail. [S72]

**Speed Round**

- Alaska's governor-elect is a Wikipedia editing fanatic, with over 13,000 edits.
- Chess.com is expanding beyond chess, launching a hub for classic games like mahjong and sudoku.
- Mark Carney's popularity is being questioned as the "Trump spell" might be breaking in Canada.
- Germany's new religious freedom report is uncharacteristically direct in criticizing China.
- Amazon's first digital photo frame is already 50% off for Black Friday, barely a month after launch.
- Researchers are warning about internet outage hell as AI forces faster system patching to combat exploit races.
- A space probe is returning to asteroids where NASA previously tested planetary defense systems.
